_readme: Every feature GATE that is OFF unless something turns it on must appear here.
The list of gates is DERIVED by AST (api/services/feature_flag_index.py) and
never typed; tests/test_feature_flag_ledger.py fails BY NAME when a new one
ships without an entry.
Why this exists: a gate that defaults off and is set nowhere is
indistinguishable, from outside the repo, from a gate that is off ON PURPOSE.
PATTERN_VISION_ENABLED=0 was a deliberate retirement; twelve others measured
on 2026-08-30 were simply never decided. Nothing could tell them apart.
status: armed  = set on at least one Railway service (its value is the decision)
dark   = deliberately off; note MUST say why
pending= built, no decision yet; note + since MUST be present
A gate can also be declared as a TABLE - a module-level *_FLAGS dict whose
keys are gate names, read in a loop. feature_flag_index learned that form on
2026-09-12, after Wave K shipped four capabilities the AST could not see:
os.environ.get(env_name) has no string constant to match, so 140 flag tests
passed over a ledger that was four gates short. tests/test_notebook_flag_table_form.py
is the rail, with the control that a bare loop-variable read is still invisible.
This file records INTENT. It cannot see Railway, so it can drift from reality:
run tools/flag_ledger_audit.py to compare it against what is actually set.
build_flags: the BUILD-TIME frontend flags, read in app/src/** as
import.meta.env.VITE_*. They are NOT in `flags` above because that section is
held to a gate list derived by AST from api/** - Python only.
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS: on 2026-09-12 nine VITE_* were set on the web service,
eight to the literal 1, and ALL NINE had been undefined in the shipped bundle
for four days (Dockerfile.web declared no build ARGs). Nothing in the repo could
see it because nothing in the repo was looking at this half of the app. That was
a structural blind spot, not an oversight.
The name list is DERIVED by tools/vite_flag_index.py and never typed;
tests/test_vite_flag_ledger.py fails BY NAME when a VITE_* ships without a row,
and tests/test_dockerfile_vite_build_args.py holds Dockerfile.web's ARG list to
the same derived set.
baked_value is a MEASUREMENT of the deployed bundle at baked_measured_on, not a
prediction. It goes stale the moment the build changes: the served JS is the
authority, and a flag read as `=== '1'` is false when undefined, which is
indistinguishable from off-on-purpose at every layer except the artifact.
flip_precondition: what must be VERIFIED before a held flag is turned on, and
what turning it on changes for a member. A flag held at 0 with no recorded
precondition is the same ambiguity as an unset one - nobody can tell whether it
is waiting on evidence or was simply forgotten.
decision / decision_reason: recorded when an owner rules on a held flag, so
the ledger says WHY a value is what it is and not merely what it is.

BREADTH_OHLC_PAGECACHE_ENABLED.note: H1 page-cache fix for the breadth deep reader (D-049). ON sets PRAGMA mmap_size=67108864 (64 MB, against a 39.9 MB file) and PRAGMA cache_size=-16000 (16 MB, against the shipped 2 MB) on every connection this module opens; OFF leaves the connection byte-identical to how it has always been opened, proved by reading both pragmas back off a real connection rather than asserting the call was skipped. ARMED ON web since 2026-09-15 on a measured A/B, not on plausibility: two production windows, identical work in both arms (rf_rows 4,529 / rf_bytes 4,523,328 on every sample), deep-cold max 11,382.4 -> 1,257.7 ms (x9.05), p90 3,052.0 -> 842.0 ms (x3.62), and the load-bearing discriminator min read-syscalls 1,669 -> 182 (x9.17) — mmap serves pages by page fault rather than read(), which is the mechanism claimed. Record: docs/breadth-history-reader/session9-report.md D.4/D.5 and docs/breadth/DECISIONS.md D-049. Rollback is the variable alone: unset it and the next boot opens connections exactly as before, no code change. WARNING - the flag was called BREADTH_OHLC_PAGECACHE until 2026-09-15 and was invisible to this ledger: is_gate() matches only names carrying a gate marker or ending _ON, so a row for the old name would have been classed as rot and would have reddened the master deploy gate. The rename is what makes this row possible AND required. Known not settled: which of mmap_size/cache_size carries the win (they ship as one flag), and the memory cost (no OFF-arm RSS baseline was captured).

BREADTH_RESIDENT_RECON_ENABLED.note: DARK, set on no service. Holds breadth_reconstructed_daily resident in the web process as {date: metrics JSON STRING}, so a deep cold read skips the 12 chunked SELECTs entirely. OFF leaves reconstructed_for_dates byte-identical to the shipped path and builds no resident object at all (asserted by the ABSENCE of the object, not by a timing). MEASURED, all 4,700 rows: resident 5,214,625 B = 1.15x the 4,523,328 wire bytes, inside the standing 2x bound; build 46 ms; invalidation is two-stage — PRAGMA data_version at 0.0034 ms on every request, falling back to a COUNT+3xMAX signature at 4.17 ms only when the file changed, against a reconstructed_fetch of 61.5 ms p50 and 975.6 ms p90. ⛔ IT HOLDS JSON STRINGS, NOT PARSED ROWS, AND THAT IS A MEASURED TRADE: parsed rows would also remove rf_materialise but cost 22,909,972 B = 5.06x wire, breaking the bound. At p90 the split is rf_fetch 607.1 ms against rf_materialise 54.4 ms, so the strings capture ~90% of the tail win for 23% of the memory; the parse stays on the request path. ⚠️ RESIDUAL: built_at has SECOND resolution, so two rebuilds inside one second with the same row count and watermarks are indistinguishable — which is why data_version is the first stage and the signature is the second. FLIP IS AN OPEN QUESTION decided on sampler data (D-051): flipping it starts a NEW pool, because rf_resident is a pooled flag and the reader changes.
